paragraphs.text: A fixed-pixel office tower for DeepSeek Harness: workspaces are floors, sessions are offices, agent
teams are the people inside.
# Pixel Office · dsh-pixel-office
A fixed-pixel office tower for **DeepSeek Harness (DSH)**: all of your sessions become one building
you can watch and click through.
> One tower = all workspaces · one floor = one workspace · one office on a floor = one session (one

agent team)
> **A lit floor means work in progress.**
English | 简体中文
## What it looks like
| All view — the tower | Workspace floor — the offices |
| Session room — the team | At night |
## Features

- **Sidebar entry next to your other panels** — a pixel tower icon opens the office page.
- **Three
zoom levels**: the whole tower (all workspaces) → one workspace floor (all of its offices) → one ses

sion room (the team). Breadcrumbs and `Esc` walk back up.
- **Live data, no refresh**: subscribes to
the host's `sessions.list` / `workspaces.list` snapshots, so running state, titles, team size, todo

progress and recent work update in place.
- **Lights mean work**: floor status strips, office windo
ws and desk lamps follow each session's `running` flag; day/night is automatic (07:00–19:00 is day)

or switchable.
- **Agent Teams aware**: the `agentTeam` projection (lead + teammates) is used when p
resent; when a projection is missing the roster is derived from the session graph (`parentId` childr
en), so future orchestrators such as Super-agent workers show up as staff too. The main session gets

the private office, teammates and subagents sit in the open office.
- **Click-through**: click a fl
oor → workspace, click an office → room, click a character → open that session; `Esc` goes up one le

vel.
- **Fixed-pixel world**: every object has a constant pixel size (floor 32, tower 420 wide, offi
ce 210×150, room core 760×488). Resizing the window reveals more or less of the office instead of st

retching it; when a page no longer fits, the pixel pager on the elevator shaft flips pages.
- **Host
-native chrome**: the page frames use the host's own `Button`, `SegmentedControl`, `Modal` and `Tool
tip` where available (with a self-contained fallback), so light/dark themes and future DSH skins kee
available (with a self-contained fallback), so light/dark themes and future DSH skins keep working.

Requires DSH **0.2.1-rc.3** or newer with the Web UI and plugin support.

3.
**From this repository** (source install):
[代码示例省略，未执行]
then install the absolute folder through DSH's plugin manager:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
4. **Local development folder**: the same `install_bundle <absolute path>` works on a checkout you e
dit; rebuild `client.js` with `node scripts/build.mjs` and refresh the window.
After installation, refresh the DSH window once so the client bundle enters the boot graph. Later cl
ient changes hot-reload in place.
## Usage

1. Click the tower icon in the left sidebar.
2. In the **All view**, each floor is a workspace; lit

offices on that floor are working sessions. Click a floor to enter it.
3. In the **workspace view**,
each glass office is a session: the lead's big desk plus the team's workstations. Click an office t

o enter the room.
4. In the **session room**, the lead sits in the private office on the right; team

mates and subagents work in the open office. Click anyone to open that session.
5. Use the day/night
switch at the top, or Settings → General → **Pixel office display**; the wheel / arrow keys / the p
ixel pager on the elevator shaft flip pages when the view has more floors or offices than fit.
## How it works
A bundle with a Host half and a Client half:
- `index.js` — Host entry; the current version only keeps the bundle shape stable for future Super-a

gent adapters.
- `client.js` — the browser module: subscribes to the session/workspace snapshots, fo
lds them into an `OfficeModel` (workspace → floors → staff), then paints three fixed-pixel scenes on
one canvas (responsive only in how much is visible). React owns the page chrome; the canvas owns th

e world.
- `cordis.patch.yml` — the bundle patch that inserts the plugin row.
No build system: `scripts/build.mjs` concatenates the owned sources in `src/` into the single-file C
lient module. `scripts/verify.mjs` runs the model and all scenes offline over several viewports, pag
es and day/night states.
## Privacy
- Only reads session metadata the host already exposes to Client plugins (titles, running state, upd

ate time, cwd, parent session, team projection, and the compact work/todo projection).
- Never reads

session log files, never writes session logs, makes no network requests and carries no telemetry.
-
One `localStorage` key: `dsh.pixel-office.display.v1` (day/night preference).
## Super-agent compatibility
The office models "who is working" as a generic session graph instead of hard-coding one multi-agent
s "who is working" as a generic session graph instead of hard-coding one multi-agent implementation:
- team leads (Agent Teams `lead`, and future `router`/`captain`/`boss` roles) sit in the boss office

;
- team-member projections, or child sessions whose `parentId` points at the session (subagents, Su

per-agent workers) sit at desks in the open office;
- role normalization and staff derivation live i
n `src/model.js`, so a new host projection or role field only needs a small adapter there; the scene
s and UI consume `OfficeModel` and never know where it came from.
## Known limitations

- The open office shows up to 6 seats; extra members appear as a “more members” chip.
- Read-only vi

sualization: no approving permissions or sending messages from inside the room.
- Below ~700 logical
pixels of width the fixed room core is cropped symmetrically (the boss office and all desks stay wh

ole; outer wall decoration is trimmed).
- Visual verification happens against a running DSH page; th
e plugin ships no preview page of its own.
